idiom_name: function component with typed hooks; stateless child typed by a props interface
implementation_notes: The typed container is a function component whose state and store subscriptions are typed at the hook boundary (useState<Line[]>, useSyncExternalStore<CartSnapshot>), rendering a child typed purely by its props interface - so a test or story can construct that props object from a literal and the compiler rejects any attempt to reach for a global. Prefer this shape in new code; the class variant remains for typed legacy code and for error boundaries.
pitfalls: A props type with optional or widened fields (any, Record<string, unknown>) lets callers omit the data the child needs; keep the interface exhaustive and its fields readonly where possible.
Generic store hooks must keep a distinct snapshot type per store - widening to one union type erases the compile-time link between a store and the children rendering it.
Module-level singletons or untyped context make the container unreplaceable in tests; inject the client through typed props or a context with an explicit test override.

variants.name: Typed class container (React.Component<Props, State>)
variants.idiom_name: class React.Component<Props, State> with typed state and lifecycle
variants.implementation_notes: The typed class form declares both contracts in its type parameters: React.Component<CartProps, CartState>, with this.state typed by the second parameter and setState checked against it. Use it when maintaining typed legacy code, for error boundaries (which have no hook equivalent) or where a lifecycle method such as getSnapshotBeforeUpdate is genuinely required; otherwise the typed function container is the default.
pitfalls: Structural typing lets a partial setState pass unnoticed when the state interface has optional fields; keep every state field required.
Overriding lifecycle methods with looser signatures, or omitting the second type parameter, disables the checks that make the class form worth typing at all.
Props copied into state stay type-correct while going stale - the compiler cannot warn that later updates are ignored.
